## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

raw_comment: In this graph, I notice that Ukraine is second in the ranking of the number of refugees from each country in one-year increases. I also notice that Ukraine is the most recent count while Ethiopia goes back to 1979 to 1980. Each time the refugee count increased in these one-year terms, a crisis has occurred in the country most likely due to war, persecution, natural disaster, or dictatorship. When looking at the lower map, I notice that most Ukrainian refugees went to Poland. This could be because their languages are similar, making it easier to communicate, and their past history together as one Republic. I wonder why people chose to go to Russia since their country is being attacked clearly by Russia specifically. It is so far out of the way compared to other countries, making it even more difficult to reach. This graph relates to me and my community because my country could be involved in the Ukrainian crisis at any time if the President decides to step in. A headline for this graph that summarizes the information given would be, "Ukrainian Refugees Count and Clear out."

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that during each year that refugees left their countries, the time period was an era of war or disagreement between countries. As a result, refugees flee to countries that neighbor their own. When examining Ukraine’s graph, it is evident that most people fled to Poland and the least traveled to Belarus. Belarus is one of the only countries that sided with Russia. Russia may have received some Ukrainian refugees because they could have family or dual citizenship with the country.
What do you wonder?
I wonder if the remainder of people in Ukraine have access (or how do they have access) to the internet/news to know where to go or what is happening. Did they know to go to Poland because it is a NATO territory?
How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to our community because each country receives and aides refugees. I also believe that the US is a diverse country that houses many different cultures, beliefs, and backgrounds. Our country should be concerned with this situation to support past refugees and welcome those who still need assistance.
What’s going on in this graph? Work with your partner to create a catchy headline that captures these two graphs’ main idea.

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |
raw_comment: I notice that there have been a very large amount of Ukrainian refugees in a relatively short period of time compared to other crises, and that the vast majority have chosen to flee into NATO countries such as Poland, Hungary and Slovakia. However, a sizable amount have also chosen to go into Russia. There are some points I wonder about, such as the percentage of the population that fled in the other crises pictured. I doubt places such as Venezuela and Rwanda have comparable populations to Ukraine, and I believe the percentage of population leaving would say more about the scale of the crisis than simply the amount. I also wonder about the relatively low influx of refugees into Romania compared to other NATO countries. As a student in an international school, this may affect the people I meet, but from the graph I can see that most are going to countries that border Ukraine, so it might not relate to me too much.

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |
